properties.decision:
Asked where the one record should live, @ajs chose "In .reflow2.toml (Recommended)" over the install receipt (git-ignored, per machine) and the store's metadata (machine-local, absent in CI). - `.reflow2.toml` takes an optional `[export] path`, relative to its folder (a directory ending in `/` for the item layout). - A file with only `[export]` names no design on a server: the folder stays a LOCAL design. - Readers: call_export.rs (after --export-to, before MCP configurations), loop_nudge's Stop hook (and it leaves the export to the writes that keep it), reflow2_init, reflow2_check.py's default, and loop_status's export standing (through call_export). - `reflow2 init --harness vscode-cli` records it, ADOPTING the export the design already keeps (an MCP configuration's --export-to, or a committed export whose graph_id is this store's) and using docs/design/

.json only when there is none. - MCP projects are unchanged unless they add the key themselves (the owner's constraint of 2026-10-05).
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-06 — a project's export path is recorded once, in the committed .reflow2.toml as [export] path, and writes, the Stop hook, init and the CI gate all read it
properties.rationale: A committed record is the only one a teammate's clone and a CI checkout both have. The receipt fixed the hook alone and only on the machine that ran init.
